description:
Read only the profiler report from the previous task and produce an executable NAS search space plan in JSON.
Behavior requirements: - Be conservative and pragmatic. - Prefer simple, well-established model families. - Include only model families clearly supported by profiler evidence. - Use small, bounded, realistic hyperparameter ranges. - Prefer categorical choices and small discrete ranges over wide continuous spaces. - Express uncertainty when profiler evidence is incomplete.
Strict constraints: - Do not inspect raw datasets. - Do not call dataset inspection tools. - Do not train models. - Do not run Optuna. - Do not evaluate model performance. - Do not select a final model.
Output must be strict JSON only (no markdown, no code fences, no prose before/after JSON).
\n\nInput: use only the profiler report generated by the previous task.

key_constraints: Small sample size (n=2,660) relative to dimensionality (d=2,500)

selected_model_families.rationale: The 2500 sequential numeric features strongly suggest a 1D signal (ECG). 1D Convolutions are effective at capturing local temporal patterns while maintaining a lower parameter count compared to dense networks, mitigating overfitting.
A standard multi-layer perceptron serves as a baseline for high-dimensional structured data. Given the relatively small sample size, a shallow MLP with strong regularization may generalize well.

uncertainty_notes: Sampling frequency of the 2500 points is unknown, making it difficult to optimize kernel sizes for specific physical durations.
Presence of 56 duplicate rows suggests potential data collection artifacts or repeated measurements.
Unknown if the signal has undergone prior filtering (e.g., band-pass) or normalization.
handoff_notes: Perform deduplication (remove 56 identified rows) before train/test splitting to prevent leakage.
Reshape input to (2500, 1) for 1D CNN architectures.
Use Stratified K-Fold cross-validation due to the small sample size relative to feature count.
Apply Global Average Pooling after 1D convolutions to reduce parameter count before the final dense layer.
